bull.b: The sharp improvement in gross margin and adjusted EBITDA indicates that recent revenue growth is beginning to translate into better operating economics. If this performance persists, it could strengthen the company’s ability to scale its gaming and marketing platform while reducing the drag from acquisition-related integration.

TubeBuddy adds a software component with materially higher cited margins than the consolidated business, while improved subscriber acquisition and activation support recurring monetization. This combination can improve the revenue mix and provide a more scalable earnings contributor as adoption develops.

A substantial locked-in revenue base and full renewal among agency-of-record clients provide evidence of customer retention and near-term commercial visibility. These characteristics can make execution more predictable, support the reiterated outlook, and reinforce the durability of GameSquare’s client relationships.

bear.b: The company remains far from sustainable profitability despite strong reported revenue growth. Deep operating and net losses, combined with negative operating and free cash flow, require continued improvement in margins and cash conversion; otherwise, growth may continue consuming resources rather than funding operations internally.

The sharp increase in leverage has reduced the equity cushion supporting the business at the same time that returns remain deeply negative. This combination increases financial risk, limits flexibility for investment or acquisitions, and makes the company more dependent on improved profitability to stabilize its capital structure.

The proposed FanEngine transaction could materially dilute existing shareholders before the acquired assets have demonstrated their contribution to earnings. Additional earnout shares and contingent cash obligations also create future capital demands, making the growth opportunity dependent on disciplined deal execution and integration.
